entries.name: Piccolo
entries.sourceReference: Dragon Ball Z, Piccolo charges Makankosappo / Special Beam Cannon with index and middle fingertips at his forehead, then releases a narrow spiral-wrapped ki beam from those two extended fingers. Purple gi corrects the near-black local reference palette. Compact effects and timings are authored adaptation, not official frames.
entries.characterVersion: Dragon Ball Z Piccolo, green Namekian with two antennae, pointed ears and pink segmented arm pads; purple gi, blue sash, brown-orange pointed boots, no cape/turban or Orange transformation.
entries.nativeCorrectionReason: Initial Special Beam Cannon rows have an overlong beam that forces the normalized body much smaller than other phases. Replace only those two action rows with native paired-finger poses and a compact coiled muzzle beam; engine VFX retain combat reach.

visualValidation.notes: Dragon Ball Z Piccolo, green Namekian with two antennae, pointed ears and pink segmented arm pads; purple gi, blue sash, brown-orange pointed boots, no cape/turban or Orange transformation. Native generated illustration and authored compact choreography. Not official-source timing or1:1 verified frames.

entries.name: Kakashi Hatake
entries.sourceWork: Naruto Shippuden, Fourth Shinobi World War Kakashi before double Mangekyo
entries.sourceReference: Naruto Shippuden, war-era Kakashi uses his single left Mangekyo Sharingan for Kamui space-time distortion. This is the pre-double-Mangekyo version, without Susanoo. The atlas depicts eye concentration and a compact grey space warp, not the electrical hand attack Raikiri. Gameplay area, timings and visual glyphs remain authored adaptation.
entries.characterVersion: War-era Kakashi before dual Mangekyo: silver spiky hair, green flak vest over navy shinobi clothes, forehead protector, black lower-face mask, gloves, white leg wraps and open-toe sandals. One left Sharingan revealed for Kamui; no Susanoo or second Sharingan.
entries.nativeCorrectionReason: The initial native atlas contains only seven actual rows, omitting the requested fatality row. A separate four-pose native Kamui finale fills that missing phase; no existing row is duplicated.
